en: The *Therāpadāna*: The Section on Seeds (Bījanivagga), No. 9, The *Apadāna* of the Elder Paduma. When I was a merchant in the city of Benares, I saw the Buddha, the peerless one among men, the Teacher who had arrived at the city. Having seen him, I gave a lotus flower to the Blessed One. Because of that root of merit, I have been reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand aeons. For eighty-four thousand aeons I have enjoyed the sovereignty of the gods. And for eighty-four thousand aeons I have enjoyed the sovereignty of kings. Having passed away from there, I was reborn in the human world. There, too, I enjoyed the sovereignty of kings. Having passed away from there, I was reborn in the Brahma-world. There, too, I enjoyed the sovereignty of Brahmā. Having passed away from there, I was reborn in the human world. Proclaiming the Four Truths,
the bringer forth of the sublime Dhamma,
he rains down the rain of the Deathless.
Bringing peace to the great multitude,
I stood in the middle of the city, holding a lotus with its stalk.
I joyfully tossed [a lotus] into the sky for the Sage Padumuttara;
and as the lotus was coming down,
It was truly wonderful at that time;
having understood my intention,
the Best of Speakers took hold of me.
Having accepted an exquisite water-born flower from Karaseṭṭha,
the Teacher stood before the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
He spoke these verses:
“By whom this lotus was thrown toward the All-Knowing Guide;”
I shall proclaim his praises;
listen as I speak.
For thirty eons, the lord of the gods—
He will exercise sovereignty over the gods;
he will dwell upon the earth, ruling the realm for seven hundred years.
There, having counted the alms-bowls,
he will become a wheel-turning monarch;
a rain of flowers fell from the sky.
Then it will rain down.
In a hundred thousand eons,
one born of the Okkāka clan;
One named Gotama by clan will become a teacher in the world;
he shall be an heir to his teachings.
Born from the heart, fashioned by the Dhamma;
having fully understood all taints,
he will attain Nibbāna, free from taints.
Having emerged from the womb,
mindful and clearly comprehending,
I was five years old by birth.
I attained arahantship.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the Venerable Elder Paduma recited these verses.
This is the ninth *apadāna* of the Elder Paduma.
